baseline.name: Materialize and sort every cross-array pair
baseline.approach: Create all m*n pairs, sort by sum, and take the first p.
baseline.space: O(m*n) pair table plus returned p pairs

archived.name: Min-heap of sorted-row frontiers
archived.time: O((r+p) log(r+1)), where r=min(nums1Size,k) and p=min(k,nums1Size*nums2Size) returned pairs
archived.space: O(r) auxiliary heap; O(p) returned pair storage and column sizes

why: Sorted inputs let the algorithm expand only the next candidate from each active row instead of storing the complete Cartesian product.
quantitative_comparison: The baseline materializes m*n pairs. This source retains r=min(m,k) heap frontiers and performs p=min(k,m*n) output-extraction cycles, each with at most a pop and next-row push. This is a storage/frontier-work comparison; no measured runtime factor is claimed.
tradeoffs: Requires sorted nonempty arrays and more involved heap/ownership code. Allocation failures are unchecked; returned rows, outer pointers and column-size storage all need caller cleanup.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
